summary: Synchronous schema preflight in function/tool invocation increases E2E latency and causes streaming disconnects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a ~2-3x increase in end-to-end latency and intermittent streaming client disconnects after enabling function/tool calling with schema validation enabled. Impact appears concentrated on requests that invoke user-defined tools (function proxies) where preflight schema checks occur synchronously before streaming tokens are forwarded.

Impact:
- Atlas Health (dedicated) sees p95 increase from ~120ms to ~400ms and p99 spikes to >1.8s for chat completions that trigger tool calls.
- Streaming clients receive ECONNRESET / premature stream close on ~3% of requests during peak traffic.
- Client application timeouts (30s) have been hit twice in the last 48h.

Environment:
- Customer: Atlas Health (dedicated capacity)
- Region: us-east-1 primary, some cross-region fallback to eu-west-1
- Models: redwood-rlhf-l2 and open-llama-3b variants used by customer
- Feature flags: tool_calls=enabled, schema_validation=enabled (default)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send chat completion with a function call that includes a complex JSON schema (~60 fields, nested objects).
2) Use streaming=true and await token stream.
3) Observe client stream open, then a pause (~300-1500ms), then tokens begin; occasional stream aborts reported.

Observed behavior:
- Additional synchronous preflight RPC from function-proxy -> validation-service occurs before server begins streaming tokens.
- Telemetry shows a ~250-900ms added serial hop in about ~30% of tool-invoke requests.
- Where validation RPC times out or is slow, client stream is closed and request surfaces as a 499/ aborted stream.

Expected behavior:
- Schema validation should be async/optimistic for streaming paths or run in parallel with initial token generation to avoid blocking first-byte latency.

Logs / traces / metrics attached: (customer supplied)
- Span trace IDs: trace-0a4f1e, trace-0a4f3c (see attached zipped traces).
- Console metrics: p95 token latency chart (link) shows inflection coincident with release 2026-03-08.
- Function-proxy logs show synchronous call to validation-service with avg RTT 320ms during peak.

Temporary mitigation suggested to customer:
- Turn off schema_validation for streaming endpoints (not ideal but reduces p95).
- Pin to a compatible model variant without nested schema usage as a short-term workaround.

Next steps requested:
- Investigate whether validation path was changed to synchronous in the 2026-03-08 runtime change.
- Determine safe async/parallel approach for validation on streaming flows.
- Provide ETA on fix and recommend a customer-safe rollback or feature flag change.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 Maya Chen (Support): Customer opened with p99 spikes and streaming disconnects after enabling tool calls. Attached traces and logs. Marked P1 due to production impact.
2026-03-10 10:05 Diego Alvarez (L2): Acknowledged. Collecting spans and asked SRE for preliminary trace correlation. Asked customer for example payload and sample request ID.

2026-03-10 13:42 SRE - Lina Park: Root traces show an added sync RPC from function-proxy to validation-service; appears to be serializing schema validation before token emission. Created INT ticket to track change (INT-237).

2026-03-11 08:30 Diego Alvarez (L2): Reproduced in staging by toggling schema_validation; confirmed latency hop. Opening PR to add async validation path for streaming: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8721. Informing customer of temporary workaround (disable schema_validation).

2026-03-12 15:00 Atlas Health - John Rivera (Customer): Disabled schema_validation per recommendation; p95 improved to ~140ms, p99 reduced significantly. Requesting timeline for permanent fix and whether any correctness risk with async validation exists.

investigation_notes: Preliminary hypothesis: a runtime change on 2026-03-08 introduced a synchronous code path to ensure schema compliance prior to token emission. This serializes the validation hop before any streaming bytes are flushed. Validation-service average latency (prod) is ~280-350ms during peak; combined with network hop explains p99 behavior. Repro in staging identical when schema_validation flag enabled. Action: instrument function-proxy to parallelize validation and emit initial tokens (first-byte) while continuing validation in background; if validation fails, emit a structured function error and allow clients to reconcile.
resolution: Escalated to runtime team; temporary feature-flag recommendation provided to customer (disable schema_validation for streaming). PR raised to add non-blocking validation path (see related PR). Ongoing work scheduled in sprint 2026-03-15 to 2026-04-02.
resolution_notes: Customer accepted workaround and confirmed improvement. Runtime team to implement optimistic validation pattern; will include audit logging and a compatibility test matrix to ensure no user-visible correctness regressions. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and update runbook to avoid future regressions when changing validation behavior.
